key_insight: The study reframes intrapartum fetal monitoring as a time-to-event prediction problem, enabling models to estimate the joint likelihood of imminent delivery and fetal acidosis from continuous CTG signals.
clinical_relevance: If validated prospectively, this approach could help identify labor risk earlier than end-of-tracing models and support more timely obstetric decision-making.
method: Built deep discrete-time survival and marked point process models for continuous physiological signals.
Predicted time to delivery alongside fetal acidosis using partially observed post-delivery labels.
Compared performance at multiple elapsed-time landmarks and tested external generalization at a second site.
evidence_signal: Marked DeepHit achieved AUROC of 0.837 at 6 hours and 0.935 at 12 hours into labor, with competitive near-delivery performance and external validation support.
watch_item: The results are retrospective proof-of-principle, so real-world usefulness still depends on prospective validation, workflow integration, and careful handling of partially observed labels.
paper_title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring
